newsitem.title: CANADA: Shell Canada plans major oil sands project.
newsitem.headline: Shell Canada plans major oil sands project.

text.p: Shell Canada Ltd., the Canadian arm of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said on Friday it planned to build the country's second-largest oil sands mining and synthetic oil project, at a cost of C$1 billion ($734 million).

Calgary-based Shell Canada said it filed with regulators plans to develop its Lease 13 in northern Alberta, in a project that would initially produce 120,000 barrels per day of bitumen -- the heavy oil in oil sands -- starting in 2002.

"This filing is the first step toward regulatory approval. We are also working hard on the technical and commercial milestones we have to meet to make this project a reality," Shell Canada vice-president Neil Camarta said.
The regulatory procedure, called a public disclosure, lets Alberta's Energy and Utilities Board know general plans for the project based on preliminary studies.

Lease 13, first acquired by Shell Canada in 1956 but never developed, is located 70 km (44 miles) north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, where the Syncrude Canada Ltd. and Suncor Inc. oil sands projects have been in operation for several years. The two now pump out enough synthetic oil to feed 20 percent of Canada's crude oil demand.
Shell Canada said it would transport its bitumen production from the project through a new pipeline, and was assessing a number of options to upgrade it into synthetic products.
Options include building a new upgrader at the company's Scotford refinery near Edmonton.

Shell Canada, which told investors last year it was considering the Lease 13 development, said it hoped to gain full regulatory approval in late 1997 and start preparing the site before the end of 1998.
